review: if i could give this place zero stars i would. the first time i went was when i broke my ankle. made us wait over four hours just to get an x-ray and we had to share a room with another patient. the next time was even worse. my girlfriend came in with abdominal pains and they made us wait three hours just to see a doctor. the doctor than told her she needed an ultrasound, which we waited two hours for and than another two for the results. after that they made her get a cat scan, which took up another two hours to get and another two for the results. than after all this doctor mchue came in for no more than thirty seconds to tell her nothing was wrong. they definitely just added procedures in order to rack up her hospital bill bordering on malpractice considering how much radiation a cat scan gives. after all this we had to wait another hour just so a nurse could come in for five seconds to take out her iv. when i went to complain to dr mchue, and told him we'd been at the hospital for almost 12 hours and we just need the iv to be taken out so we could go home, he rudely told me "people are dying." i understand that it's an emergency room but there were atleast ten people talking or sitting at their computers, one of which is capable of removing an iv, or dr mchue should've just done it himself when he came to see us. his attitude was not one any dr should have and it was clear he got stuck with the graveyard shift and was not happy about it. terrible terrible doctor. don't go unless you're literally dying because they will not help you. go to a different hospital if you can and definitely hope to god you don't get dr mchue, because i've never encountered a more rude or dismissive dr in my life. fuck this p

i will say, i haven't received my bill yet which i'm slightly nervous for - but i trust they'll have a great billing department. we were on vacation in wa when we were transported by ambulance to tacoma children's hospital. from the er to the last day we were here people were amazing. my daughter was have severe trouble breathing due to a severe case of croup, virus and bacterial infection. they were fast and efficient about getting her started on the meds she needed right away. dr. mccabe & dr. williams were the ones who were assigned to us, they were absolutely amazing! after thinking about it, i was so happy that we were in wa when this happened and not at our home (ca). because i can guarantee the care we received wouldn't have been able to compare to out in la.

it's never fun when you end up in the er. check in ran smoothly, but of a wait since lots of sick kiddos but it's that time of year with the flu and all. very grateful that people were wearing their face masks and all. 

once i got a bed it went pretty quickly, had my xrays and meds and the cool app that tells you the progress of the tests was so awesome! i really do like that new feature. 

but the bad happened as i was leaving :( i was given a  hospital gown to wear because i had a lot of x rays to take,  i mean i sprained my entire body from the fall i had. miracle i didn't break anything. anyway, the hospital gown had dry blood in the inside. i was not bleeding so this grossed me out  and my husband. immediately told the doctor and my nurse. they just said they'd wash it again, my husband said  they should throw it away. i was too drugged on percocet and muscle relaxers to argue. 

other than that i'm healing and feel better.  i do wish that the tree given to me at the end with my diagnosis was just given to me via  a link in that cool  app.

went in to see what's was wrong with me and three of my kids we all can not keep anything down and all of our temperature were above 100. they didn't do much but say it was a virus. only got our blood pressure, height, and weight done so how do they know if that is the problem. my daughter is two years old and cannot even walk without shaking. 

- 0 stars

update: still visiting as part of my ministry. with all the worries of flu and coronavirus, they still have empty hand sanitizing stations, dirty bathrooms, and no soap in some dispensers. really? this is sad. when do they plan on correcting this? this is my third update in only a couple of years, and still, they have not fixed the problem. please be aware of this. your health could be at risk! too no avail, i mentioned to staff before. is it apathy, laziness, or lack of concern? sad!

review: i'm in my late 40s. i am a former soldier. i have been to emergency rooms around the world. i was a paramedic for years. this was the wooooorst medical experience i have ever had. i have had my face reconstructed. i have been shot. i was unfortunate enough to experience the worse pain i have ever had in my life for the second time, another kidney stone. i knew exactly what it was. i told these assholes exactly what it was. i'm have insurance out the whazoo. but yet, these assholes let me roll around their nasty ass floor in pain for hours without once attempting to manage my pain. i didn't want any narcotics. i wanted toradol to open my vessels. i walked out twice because they refused to move with any sense of urgency to get me relief. listen to what i said, i walked out twice because they were disinterested in helping me in my severe distress. like i wanted to be in the emergency... i should not have been in this emergency room thinking i should shoot myself to get more expedited care. i didn't go through with it because they still probably wouldn't give me the toradol.... i walked out in severe pain, went to north richland hills emergency room, was in a bed in 10 minutes, got a shot of toradol in another 15 minutes, and past the stone in my urine sample within the hour...i pray to the lord that something replaces the triage nurse and doctor in harris methodist er, to include the corona virus.

review:
this is hands down the most ghetto kaiser i've ever had the displeasure of going to with more hipaa violations then i could count! i checked in at the front to a woman who barely spoke english out of a box with bullet proof windows & she didn't use her speaker to converse so checking in was a pain and it felt like i was at a shady 7/11 in a questionable side of town... they finally pull me to the back and ask me questions as i just had surgery on my hand a few days prior. 

i was then taking back to the waiting room (nurses were chatting & gossiping to themselves several minutes & complete informing the pa trying to get me a seat) and put in this little quarantine style cubicle with a complete unobstructed view of people checking into security peering through the window! after an hour finally a dr assistant checks on me, and unwraps my bandage with several people staring in & looking at my hand that's healing. that was beyond disrespectful, degrading and completely breaking so many hipaa laws for patient privacy. wtf said this was a good idea, they need to be fired. 

nurses were literally yelling out my information to each other about my condition where other patients could hear, another clear cut hipaa violation! then to top of off i went another hour and a half without anybody updating me on anything so i ask a male nurse is there an eta & he said they may be in surgery and for me to wait, i told him i've been here for 3 hours now with no update on anything, he then said i can "feel free to leave whenever i want, nobody is forcing me to stay here," as i'm recovering from surgery 3 days prior.

i wasnt feeling well so my husband took me to the emergency room.  it was busy and we waited for about 5 hours. when i got to my room in the er the doctor was very blunt and to the point, almost on the verge of rude. but shelby my nurse was amazing! so sweet and funny, she really did make it easier.  my blood test was off so her ordered an ultrasound and a ct scan. those were done right away and about an hour after shelby came in to start an iv line. i asked why and she said oh because you're having surgery soon, didnt the doctor come in and tell you? ummm no he didnt! when i got admitted and they were about to take me to my room he literally popped his head in and said "i'm sure you know by now that you're having surgery.  your gallbladder is not doing great so it needs to be removed." oh ok thanks. worst bedside manner ever. 
they got me to my room, and i understand that it's not a hotel and we cant really pick and choose, but they put me in with an elderly lady who had pneumonia and some other things going on and was highly contagious.  why would you put someone who is healthy and about to have surgery in with someone who is super sick?! i had some stuff going on with me that caused me to be quarantined so they ended up moving her. my husband asked if they could have someone come in and clean the bathroom since she was up and about all over the room and they said sure. nobody ever came and we ended up doing it ourselves (good thing there were purple wipes outside my door!) 
we were originally told that i was scheduled for surgery first thing in the morning, then my surgeon came in and said it would be around 10am. that was the last we heard all day. we kept asking when they would be taking me in and nobody had a clue. the lack of communication was phenomenal.  i ended up being the last surgery of the day because apparently my surgeon is a pushover and others kept pushing us back since they knew he wouldn't get mad.(my nurses words not mine.) meanwhile i got to sit in extreme pain not being able to eat or drink. not even water. after surgery i wasnt feeling too great and i asked for pain meds at midnight. i didnt get them until 4am. horrible. i had to beg for one of those sponges to wet my lips because i still wasnt allowed to eat or drink and when the aide finally said yes he watched me like i was a criminal to make sure i didnt drink any water. horrible. i waited until 9pm the next day for the dr to come in and see me and he ordered an mri for the next morning. they took me at about 745am and that went fine...until they left me in the hallway for 45 minutes after the mri! the tech walked by and i asked if they were going to take me back and he said "oh they haven't taken you back yet?" hmmm...wow! there were other things that happened but i will leave it at that for now. this was by far the worst experience i have ever had here. i strongly recommend going somewhere else if you need any services(other than having a baby...in that respect they're pretty awesome). only reason for two stars is because the nurses i had were really nice.

what has happened to this hospital??  my husband has been here many times, and most visits were good, except for the extremely long waits in the er.  my husband had surgery on friday and stayed overnight.  he just finished chemotherapy, so his immune system has been wiped out.  they obviously didn't consider this at all, or didn't care; so they gave him a room in the old wing where more than half the patients in the unit were quarantined!!  there were warning signs on the doors, but the doors were left open, so germs and bacteria could freely travel throughout the ward.  the nurses were unfriendly and unattentive.  my husband had to go looking for his nurse, pat, twice, and found her visiting in the corridor.  he was released by the surgeon the morning after surgery, but it took several hours for the nurses to complete the paperwork.  he was given no breakfast, and no explanation, even though it was allowed.  he was told he would be given lunch before leaving, and he had to ask about it three times before he was finally given a tray.  his "lunch" was an omelet full of eggshells!  obviously someone's breakfast that they didn't want.  he was in excrutiating pain, but they refused to give him pain medication because the doctor's orders had already been written.  he told the nurse how severe his pain was, and instead of offering to call the doctor for permission to dispense more pain medication, she asked if she should call the doctor for permission to stay in the hospital another night, knowing that no one would volunteer to stay one more night in that terrible situation.  we are very upset and disappointed that the hospital has changed so drastically.  i see from the other reviews that this experience was not a one-time exception; it has become the norm.

around 2:30 am the sunday before thanksgiving, my mother was having severe dizziness & couldn't move without the room spinning.  she went by ambulance to st. mary's medical center hospital in langhorne.  

the nurse who hooked her up to the iv caused pain & swelling in my mom's hand while trying to get the needle in.  the ed doctor couldn't wait to send her home after giving her meds via the iv & pills then telling her she was okay to go.   while being wheeled out she began to vomit violently.   luckily the nurse/assist had compassion, helped her back into bed & said he'd inform the dr.  they hooked her back up to the iv & admitted her, but there were no beds available.  finally in the afternoon she was placed in a room.

tuesday afternoon when i came back.  my mom had uncontrollable diarrhea, soiled her clothes, bed, floor, & practically every surface in the bathroom .   i told her there was no way she was leaving the hospital & was in no condition to go home.  she said they already confirmed she's staying, expected to be released tomorrow morning, & they took a culture.  

wednesday morning it's confirmed she has the norovirus & will be released first thing thanksgiving morning.  we believe she contracted the norovirus after being admitted to st. mary's medical center hospital in langhorne on sunday.    i came to visit, see a sign by her room door  instructing visitors to report to the nurses station.  i approached the nurse's station; explain who i am, who i'm visiting, which room, & the sign.  i was told to put on gloves & smock that are on the wall by the door.  never doing this i asked for assistance only to get silence from the nurse's station as they watched me struggle.   the morning housekeeping woman is the one who explained the process to me.  my mom spent the night with the stench of feces coming from her uncleaned smelly bathroom.   she  told me that the night shift housekeeping woman walked in, opened the bathroom door, sighed, closed the door & walked out never to return.   my mom said the morning housekeeper came in to tidy up only to find the disgusting bathroom that had fecal matter still on the floor, walls, sink & toilet.    i told my mom to watch tv & she said she didn't want to pay.  as i left the hospital a visitor told me tv is free in patient's rooms.  i asked my mom's nurse why no one explained that tv was free.  the nurse said "she never asked".  my mom was given headphones for the tv on wednesday, but no one told her how/where to plug them in. 

thanksgiving morning i kept checking to see if she was released as they said they were sure she wanted to be home for thanksgiving.    she said she was fully dressed & the iv disconnect but was waiting for the dr. orders to go thru.  it wasn't until early afternoon when she wanted to sign herself out that they finally came in with her discharge papers.  

my mom was treated like a nonentity while she was a patient.  she was never given a welcome packet, never given her patient bill of rights.  nothing was ever explained to her.  i called patient advocacy on wednesday to complain about the lack of information only to be told "all we can do is make suggestions".   the patient advocate concierge did visit my mom on wednesday but only gave her a welcome packet containing substance abuse literature. 

after my mother's release, i called & spoke with the patient representative who was compassionate & apologetic.  i later received a call from the nurse manager of the floor my mother was on.  she told me that we should have called the number on the white board in my mother's room.  again, that wasn't explained to her or me while my mother was a patient.  it would have been helpful to know.    the nurse manager did tell me she will review my mother's concerns with their nursing team as they could have done a better job.

i have already placed a call to hospital administration to make them aware of the subpar treatment we received, but i also want to make certain the public is aware as well. please do  not waste your time at this emergency dept. i highly recommend going to savannah as we should have done, but our son was very sick so we stopped here rather than proceeding to savannah. he had been diagnosed w type b flu on monday. our doctor encouraged us to return or take him to an er/urgent care if after hours if he became worse. in the early morning hours of wednesday he became much worse; screaming in pain, unable to feel his legs below the knees, and a spike in fever despite tylenol  & motrin, and began vomiting. we rushed him to coastal carolina er.  from the second we stepped in the door the treatment we received was inexcusable. the check in person yelled across the room to ask what was wrong as we were struggling to get him in the door. i explained
he had been diagnosed w flu earlier in the week & she simply threw a mask at me rather than offering some help to get him in. the triage nurse was hateful and also offered no help.  she put us in a cold room w no sheet or blanket on the bed and left. we were then greeted by an extremely hateful  dr sutherland who asked why we were there. we explained what was going on, his diagnosis, & then she asked what we expected her to do as this was common for the flu.  we explained our doctor told us to immediately have him seen if he became worse which he did, which is why we were there.  she looked at me & left the room. the triage nurse returns, does not bother to tell us what she's giving him until i ask. she gives him zofran and tylenol/motrin & leaves. my son was absolutely freezing so i walk to nurses desk to ask for a blanket & hear them discussing the fact of how ridiculous they think it is that we brought our son to the er. (i am fairly certain this is a hippaa violation...we have contacted the governing board as well). she snaps at me that she's "fixin  to discharge him" (her exact words) so a blanket wont be necessary.  i realize it was nearing the 7am shift change  but this lack of care our  son received is completely inexcusable. we will never return to this facility and will discourage anyone from visiting this er.

review: brought my mom is a few months ago (before the coronavirus) because she couldn't regulate her temperature due to her cancer treatments. the nurse kept saying we were safer to stay home. i get it! we are surrounded by sick people but she was covered in blankets and heating pads and felt like she was going to freeze. when she finally got a room days later the nurse was more concerned about the paperwork than my mom. she asked us the same questions we already answered three times before about her medications and medical history. mom started to get chills again which is always followed by a high fever. i told her and that tylenol would do the trick. she wouldn't give it to her bc the fever hadn't spiked yet. it's just tylenol!!! she kept asking her questions but by then my mom was delirious and couldn't even say her own name! she kept saying she was fine and just tired. i begged for tylenol but they refused. they used the external temperature and it was 99. they said they will wait till it got to 100 to give her tylenol. i brought my own oral thermometer and it read 102. finally i had to call the head nurse to get help and by then her fever was 103!!!! this is the worst place! i hope that nurse gets fired!!! they had no regard for my moms well being and we will never go there again.

what was going on. too many doctors taking care of one person. none of them were on the same page . the third floor was the only decent part of this experience, we had one nurse named christina and she was amazing and we are thankful for her help.

(12/28/19; better get my last 2019 reviews done!) 

being from san leandro, my family and i were happy to see this place develop over the years. today, it is an expansive hospital and healthcare facility, complete with all the kaiser fixings of a lab, pharmacy, and specialty physicians for all seasons. 

i have a history with this place. i once enjoyed a fascinating stay at the er for an injury that would make for a good story some other time. suffice it to say, this kaiser permanente has long earned my trust and confidence. 

on this particular morning, all i needed was a little blood work. i requested an elective test, and my doctor in union city obliged by ordering it for me. it required an early hour of arrival, which initially concerned me since a lot of blood work is often scheduled for the mornings (fasting glucoses, hormones, and so forth). however, when i arrived at 8:00 a.m. on this saturday morning, i was pleased to find that i was the only patient there! 

i drew a number, checked in shortly thereafter, and within a minute i was already seated -- a phlebotomist being drawn by another phlebotomist. we had a pleasant chat about venipuncture and how cold the weather was outside, and before i knew it, our work was done! best of all, i got my results that very evening. 

that'll do, kaiser san leandro. it's always a pleasure for me to visit this facility. in the highly unlikely event i were to move back to the bay area, it would be an honor to practice medicine here, or any of the other kaiser offices. nonetheless, being a patient is more than fine by me, and when i'm next in town, i know where to go for my healthcare needs. until then!

review:
hopefully you read this before going to the er, not after like i did.  reading some of the other reviews - similar things happened to me.

on friday february 28th at about 8:30pm my daughter and i took our 18 month old grandson to the emergency room on bee ridge and cattlemen.  

1.  my daughter was holding the baby who was crying - he had been bitten on the hand by a dog.
2.  the security guard never looked up from his computer and mumbled for us to sit down - "they know you're here."  we were the only people in the er, so i'm thinking "who knows we're here?"
3.  three women were behind a desk and did not make eye contact with us - no concern for a young woman holding a crying baby.  they just talked to each other - nobody told us anything.
4.  five minutes becomes 10 minutes and nobody said anything to us.
5.  after about 10-12 minutes a door marked triage opens and some patient comes out.  the triage nurse asked us to come in.
6.  she did not wash her hands, use purell, or wear gloves.
7.  she had to do all the typing to get us into the system (i guess the other three women were busy not helping)
8.  after about 15 questions - she finally asked why we were here.  we told her he had been bitten by a dog.
9.  when she reached for his hand - he of course screamed - so she reached for an unsanitized teddy bear on her desk and gave that to him to quiet him down.
10.  she dabbed the wound clean (did not rinse it) and moved us through some double doors into another waiting room with about six chairs - again we were the only people there.
11.  about another 10-15 minutes later a nurse came in and confirmed the baby's name.  then she asked us if he had a fever?  no?  a cough?  no?  we told her he had a dog bite.  (i wonder why she hadn't read the triage report??)
12.  she asked my daughter a dozen questions which had nothing to do with the dog bite, including vaginal or c-section delivery?  i'm guessing that is a priority when treating a dog bite.
13.  another 10 - 15 minutes and a doctor came into the room.  and here's where i started to question this whole operation.  he never came closer than 10 feet from the baby - never looked at the wound, let alone cleaned it.  from 10 feet away he then described what he was going to do - he was going to order an x-ray and then give us some antibiotics - because he told us without antibiotics the risk of infection is very high.
14.  another 10-15 minutes and a guy from x-ray came and told us he had been instructed to an x-ray of the right hand.  "is this _____?"  good guess!

did you ever see the movie zootpia where she has to go to the dmv to get her license?  that's what this experience brought to my mind.  they were like the sloths but without the smile and the compassion.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=drhsktakrzc 

15.  another 30 minutes and the nurse came back asking us what was happening.  that is when i got a little frustrated and asked her why the doctor had not even looked at the wound?  why hadn't the wound been cleaned?  she seemed to think that the doctor had looked at the wound.
16.  i could go on and on...

finally the nurse came back with the prescription for the antibiotic - it was now 11 at night.  i asked her if she could call in the prescription so it would be ready when we got there.  "we don't provide that service."

this is a perfect example of an organization which is driven by procedure - and has absolutely no focus on patients.  no compassion, no coordination, no communication.  the system these people work in has crushed their humanity - and this is with an empty er.

all the while i'm thinking to myself - "omg imagine if there was a corona virus outbreak in sarasota and there were five or six puking sick people in the er waiting room?  this hospital is completely unprepared to handle anything like that."

come to find out two days later that there was a corona virus patient in the hospital that night - and i thought back to the people not washing their hands, etc. etc.  i pray that my grandson, my daughter and i were not infected.  

and hannah b. don't respond "i am so sorry to hear about your experience..."  if you gave a damn, you would go to the er yourself and see what your customers see - it isn't pretty.  if you did care, it would either be fixed, or you wouldn't be working there.

review: this is in reference to the outpatient intensive therapy day program. i was really at a low when i entered into this program. prior to entering i was very afraid. after being there for some time it felt safe. the staff members are very helpful and resourceful. they are willing to assist in whatever your need may be at the time. it may be a little uneasy on your first few days because you have to get to know people and be comfortable enough to want to share your story. you are never forced to do anything. this is a very intensive program. i suggest if you are not ready to do the work to help you heal this is not the program for you. the program teaches numerous skills that can aid in getting a grip on your mental illness. on the outside you may feel like an outcast. this is one place you can come and not be obligated to wear a mask. meaning you can be yourself. you have the opportunities to listen to others story. you also have the opportunity to share your story. you receive plenty of advice and suggestions. there is a daily schedule. first meeting with your nurse to discuss the daily questionnaire you must complete each morning. next you move on to a class with your social worker. once that is completed you continue with 4 more daily classes. the day starts at 8:30 am and ends at 3:20 pm. the program is monday thru friday. if you are truly ready to learn more about your illness and are ready to apply learned skills this program may be for you. i appreciate what is being taught there and look forward to using the learned skills to make coping with my illness easier.

(he was seen by a geneva practitioner and released, stating it was just a gastrointestinal bug) they went to geneva, the boy died under their care. he had peritonitis.
do not go here!!!

this hospital used to be wonderful. since being taken over by nyu it's abundantly clear that it's profits over patients. the hospital is over run with interns and residents. they don't even read your chart when they come into the room and you have to tell the same story over and over and over again. 3 of them will come in and want to take turns checking your already upset toddler. my daughter came in with a stomach virus with dehydration and low blood sugar. the interns and residents treated her symptoms but had zero regard for anything else i was telling them. they dismiss the mothers who know their babies best. the nurses, child life specialists and other staff were wonderful but the "doctors" in the pediatric unit are terrible. i was told they wouldn't run anymore tests because it's a waste of hospital resources.  i will never return to winthrop again.

how osha didn't shut down this hospital yet is beyond me. a nurse removed my iv without gloves, make matters worse. it was during the corona outbreak scare. i was laying in a hospital bed without a diagnosis but taking meds and had an iv in. so what was i being treated for when no one knew what my diagnosis was.

i had to ask, (two days later) what my diagnosis was and what i was being treated for.  finally, after much debate, they sent me for a ct scan which is the boilerplate basic protocol if you ask me. the medical professional school rejects from all walks of life work here. buyer beware! run!!! do not go here if you can help it.

hospital food is awful, worse when most of the food looks like something i wouldn't even feed my dog.

yesterday was a first time experience with the adult er, and it was pretty great!  my elderly mother has a lot of urinary issues, and her urologist sent us to the er.
there was a two hour wait, to be expected at this time of the year.  love the accessibility of masks, since the waiting area was full of the flu.  once we went through triage, everything moved right along. 
loved the communication  between the er dr. and my mothers urologist, he had good insight before he even spoke to us.   the only thing i could say that could have been better was that the nurse could have been better at listening, she was in the zone.  i understand the busyness in that setting,  but details about the patient are important.  we left with a plan in place, my mother felt good about it.  i would definitely use williamson medical again, beats going downtown.

rushed my mother to williamson medical at 1 am this morning hoping to get relief from the writhing pain she was experiencing related to bladder cancer. despite having only one other patient, the er team was cold, harsh, thoughtless and entirely lacking in empathy. they were also mistaken in key parts of their diagnosis and their treatment. 

based on my experience today, i would never send a relative or a friend to williamson medical under any circumstance imaginable. 

why do these "healthcare professionals" feel they are serving their patients if they allow interminable delays (we were left for 2 hours without getting pain medication of any kind - the very reason we went in the first place) and brutish bedside manners (being moved from bed to gurney like a sack of potatoes, my mother getting screamed at during insertion of a catheter, blaming the patient for difficulty finding a vein {it took 3 tries and 3 pokes} in which to insert an iv, etc.).  10-minutes into the nurse screaming catheter insertion i heard the head nurse, amy, finally ask my mother what her name was. think about that. 

i found medical trash strewn all over the room we were in. this is 3rd world treatment and 3rd world quality care. 

i have great reverence for those who commit their lives to the serving and healing of strangers. i revere and feel hfriends who are er doctors, social workers, cancer scientists. these people serve mankind and they have empathy somehow baked into their dna. the er team at williamson medical should seriously consider why they chose to serve the public. i wouldn't hire any of the nurses or the doctor we dealt with to deliver my mail - they'd find a way to screw it up. they might, however, be just right to pick up our trash curbside.

to be fair, i should note we had generally positive experiences from the er check-in staff. also had acceptable treatment and care after getting my mother checked into the main hospital. but by the time we were upstairs, we had lost faith in the entire place, so we were watching/prodding them closely to be sure they attended properly to our mom. no one should need to do that. 

later in the day i spoke to an emt who said he wouldn't allow his friends or family to get taken to williamson medical er, that they have an awful reputation as a dumping ground for patients who have no advocacy and no close family oversight. his quote was "tell them to take you farther north to vandy, st. thomas etc. ". he also said, "even if you arrive at williamson medical without an infection, you'll surely leave with one". yikes.  wish i'd known. that's why i've labored over this review. beware. 

and my heart goes out to anyone reading this who has a loved one suffering like my mother has. god bless.

i took my friend to the er last thursday. she was in excruciating head pain and vomiting. we got there at 4:00 pm. it was very busy. the nurses and doctors are kind. however, no one saw her for two hours. by 7:00 she had an x-ray. no one addressed her migraine. no one addressed  her vomiting. her spouse came at 6:30pm . i went home at 7:00pm. by 12:00 am they finally gave her some pain meds and an i.v.  eight hours of suffering in the  er surrounded  by very sick people, many vomiting. my friend did not have the flu. the next day i was violently ill for 24 hrs. my doctor thought it was a virus but perhaps food poisoning. my husband and i ate the same food and he was fine. i think i got ill from  being in the er four hours even though i wore a mask ( which is probably useless in preventing flu virus from penetrating). 

i would  not recommend los robles hospital emergency room if you are sick. go to urgent care or stay home and wait it out. 

btw she's allergic to penicillin and they gave her an antibiotic very similar to penicillin. she had  to go to urgent care the next day to get a steroid shot to combat the  allergic reaction (hives) she had from the antibiotic they gave her in er.

also, i  suggest you investigate the  hospital's reporting of infections gotten in the hospital.

as you can tell if you look at how often i write reviews, i am extremely selective in my assessments. to cause me to write a review means you either hit a home run, or you struck out. unfortunately it's the latter with the emergency room of this hospital. we live within walking distance, and have lived in the community for 20 years +. in that time, we've used the hospital or the er just once or twice.  in other words, we're healthy, use regular doctors to meet our basic health needs, and are not the type of people who run to the er for a paper cut. additionally, we have truly excellent insurance supplied by our employers. 

with that as background, we visited the er at 1 am this week. my husband had been flat on his back with the flu/cold since returning from texas about 10 days ago. he was running a fever, coughing frequently, hadn't been able to eat, and was having trouble breathing. when we checked in we explained his symptoms and told them several times he'd been in international airports since coronavirus was starting to be talked about. when the er doctor sat down, he asked my husband "what's going on?" my husband very reasonably responded to that question by saying "i think i have the flu." the doctor shot back "i'll make the diagnosis." that sums up our experience in the er. they were generally detached, rude, and acted like we were bothering them by being there. the one exception was the truly friendly guy with the portable machine he rolled around to get a bit more info from patients such as religious preference. but the nurses and the doctor were awful. they didn't follow up with us about my husband being in houston airport (where the coronavirus was found), and when he complained about being lightheaded they initially ignored him and then reluctantly offered a wheelchair. they also debated between themselves as to whether they should offer an inhaler. once concluded, one trotted off to find the doctor. the other disappeared without telling us anything. a third employee sat staring at his phone, tapping away, and never said a word to us or looked our way even though we were perhaps 3 feet from him. i was standing the entire time and none offered me a chair.

as a community member, i don't feel los robles provided even minimally acceptable service. i looked on their website for a place to lodge complaints but there isn't one. interesting. additionally, there are more "1" ratings of this hospital on this site than "5" ratings. i'm not surprised by that.  i'm sure there will be an insipid follow up comment from jasmin o. saying "thank you for your comment, sorry we didn't meet your expectations" or something noncommittal like that. the fact that the hospital offers the same canned response to every poor review indicates to me that there is a lack of true caring.

everyone has bad days at work, i get that. but in certain industries, that can be dangerous. you don't want ticked off air traffic controllers, lackadaisical nuclear energy plant operators, or medical staff who lack compassion and don't really want to help patients. i expected more out of the er. we won't return; we'll go to an urgent care spot if needed in the future. which is too bad since los robles loses a future chance to over bill our very generous insurance company.

bottom line, i don't recommend anyone willingly going to this hospital's er based on our experience this week.

how can you truly rate a hospital? based off of skill of drs/surgeons/np/nurses/cnas? of quality of care? quality of food(which we all know who have been in a hospital for any extended time can be atrocious)? how about all of the above!

i was admitted on 11/7 for a major surgery. not simple by any means and i am glad and blessed that this was the hospital i went to. aortic valve replacement which entails open heart surgery is scary enough to hear, but the team here at sharp memorial along with my surgeon dr. adamson put my fears to rest. from the initial consultation with him and going over what was to occur i felt at ease along with my girlfriend. even making jokes with me to relax me and calm my nerves just showed the bedside manner was well above par.

the complex is large and if you have multiple appointments in different buildings as i did. just ask the nurse assisting you to request a shuttle and they will get you to were you need to go. instead of moving your car over and over and dealing with the parking.

depending on what you're in for will dictate what floor/building you will be placed in. post op recovery icu is 2nd floor of main building and god bless if that's what you're in for.

nursing staff along with the np(nurse practitioner, don't call them a dr even if they're right there) have some of the most gentle care i've experienced from any hospital. i've bee. to other sharps and i can wholeheartedly say this hospital takes the prize. from providing you with as much information as possible to assist you in your recovery to ensuring you help is merely a call away by providing you with their direct number(they're given a cell phone at work so they can be reached by you or the nurses station if needed urgently) these ladies and gentleman embody care. my hats off to floor 6 (cardiac recover) for all the outstanding service and care they provided me. i honestly don't think i would have been recovering as well as i am without their support and care.

food is still none the less hospital food but i was able to speak with the chef in charge and here their plans for the coming year. adopting a comprehensive plan to ensure that the food quality and nutritional value are in keeping with the care provided at the hospital. a one of a kind program that already has made staples in improving the quality of the food and nutritional value(small steps so far such as switching from iceberg lettuce to green leaf lettuce and such). my hats off to them for improving this overlooked aspect in hospitals. the ordering system is fantastic how they take your meal order ahead of time to not interfere with your recovery and to ensure that you designated meal with restrictions if any get to you on time. i lived how each .real came with a nutritional overview letting you k ow nutrients, calories, etc in your meal. loved that!

radiology/radiologist as i had to deal with frequently were friendly and helpful. whether they had to assist me in my room or take me down to get mris(be aware, its always the coldest part of the building because they do have to keep those machines cool or they can burnout so ask for bra blanket if you need it). the transport team who assisted you getting from location to location or helping you leave in the end were always kind, helpful and made sure you knew you were always welcomed back.... hopefully not soon though.

all in all if i could rate this hospital a 11 or higher i would! excellent is the only word i can come up with to describe the care provided by the staff at sharp memorial. my hats off to all the staff that help in the recovery of the many patients who walk through their doors and the supporting staff behind the scenes.

i had my first kidney stone experience ever and was in so much pain i decided to call the ambulance to help take me straight to the emergency. worst mistake of my life...
3:00pm: the austin ems ambulance is a joke taking more than 30 minutes to arrive to pick me up, two heavy built male medical ems staff took me into the vehicle and started interviewing and collecting my information, taking their sweet time parking at one place not driving me to the hospital for another 30 minutes. i have to beg for pain meds and they gave a shot for it but poorly directed the needle causing me unbearable pain i literally scream from so much pain!
4:30pm: the ambulance arrived at st david's south austin er walk-in, to my surprise i did not immediately get to see the doctor but had to wait in line to be checked in! omg, the torturous wait and the unbearable pain. i asked if i can have a bed to wait, no, sitting hurts me so much i cried the whole time waiting...
5:30pm: i had to go the bathroom and they called my name finally but i was in too much in pain to run out so i crawled out slowly and they told me i have to wait again because they skipped me! why did they not check the bathroom???
5:50pm: they called my name i thought i was finally saved, but a nurse took me inside a chair just to collect my insurance info and gave me a name tag, then sent me back out to wait some more. i begged for more pain meds as the old pain meds worn out, no, they cannot give me any meds until i see a doctor...at this time i'm heavily considering laying on the floor due to so much pain. i threw up 3 times in the bathroom and was heavily dehydrated, i begged a nurse for some water, he said he will go get me some, he never came back...i had to drink some water from the bathroom sink to stay alive. i continued crying in pain waiting and no tears came out since i'm so dehydrated....
6:50pm: they called my name again i thought i was finally saved again, but this time they took me to a chair to put iv on me to draw my blood and get urine test only. the nurse lady was so incompetent she had to poke me twice to find my vein, the first time she was probing with the large needle giving me excruciating pain while watching how incompetent she was. she continued to probe me the second time i felt like i should just die already, blood splatters everywhere and i saw old blood stain under the chair...still refused to give me water but agreed to give me pain meds finally. i beg for a bed, no, they have no bed available and i have to continue to wait in the waiting area. i got fever chills after all the blood drawn and beg for a blanket, no, they can't give me blanket to prevent contamination...no water, no blankets, no ability to lay down, no time frame to see doctor, constant excruciating pain, i was ready to just die...
7:30pm: finally got a bed, right out in the hallway with a number on the hallway wall. still not allow me to drink any water, a new nurse came to take more blood samples from me, poking and probing at my small veins at multiple places half jokingly complained my vein was so tiny (i'm so dehydrated of course my vein is tiny!!!). gave me ct scans, and concluded i got kidney stone...
10:00pm: gave me some prescription drugs, made me signed a bunch of forms to pay medical bills when it comes and dismissed me...

i've never been treated so badly in my life! 5.5 hours of torture! austin ems and this er sees me as nothing but a number and an object to poke at and probe without feelings...gravely disappointed at the american health system, and to say we are fully prepared for covid19, what a joke!

then no one helped with the wheel chair throughout the entire stay.  additionally i have never seen a hospital run in this fashion where patients are treated in front of everyone in a seperate waiting room. it felt to me like an invasion of their privacy and fight almost broke out in that room as well.

coronavirus is less deadly than this hospital. piss poor service. i have a preexisting back injury and had to go in because i could not deal with the pain anymore. the nurses are garbage. they rush you out and state all your business in front of everybody. that is a privacy policy violation. i have to get a second opinion and a lawyer now because they can't do their job.

this happened a while ago but it has stuck with me as completely worth putting out there. first time i saw the doctor. i found the nurse practitioner was better than the doctor, initially. i went about 3 times to np with o.k. results, probably because i was asking for referrals. she often questioned my medical history. initially, i gave her the benefit of the doubt because my history is rather lengthy for someone my age. i thought that maybe she was wanting to check something. now i know it wasn't any of that and she was falsely judging my issues. on the 4th visit when she denied me help with lower back pain which was causing a lot of fatigue and said she didn't know where to refer me and so gave me a blood test. feeling a little in shock i just went along with her ordering a blood test for vitamin deficiency, when i knew it was because the pain was serious. when they were taking my blood in the lab in the back, i could hear the nurse practitioner talking about me negatively to the staff around the desk. you're lucky i wasn't feeling well or i would've confronted you and reported you to the nursing board for confidentiality violation. it turned out i needed physical therapy for several things she totally missed. the doctor and nurse practitioner were incompetent. the nurse practitioner was also unprofessional.

this is regarding the er. i was incredibly disappointed with the care received. my little sister fainted while in the shower during her period. she had a small gash on her head-- because it was on her face we wanted to make sure there was no scarring and thus took her to the er. when we got there, they checked us in... and called us to the back for an ekg and blood work (excessive, yes, but it is the er). they took us back to the front, and called us back again for a chest x-ray. the np was walking by so we inquired as to why a chest x-ray was needed for someone who fainted (with known cause) after an ekg was already done.  the np proceeded to tell us that football players have fainted and died (completely irrelevant). i asked her if the ekg was normal, and her response was that there was syncope and we needed to find the cause of the syncope. then she asked my 18 yr old sister if she felt a vagal response. i looked up what syncope was on my phone- "fainting"? why is a medical professional using these terms when talking to patients? terrible bedside manner. my sister had to ask what she meant, and she still was unable to explain properly. i asked if my sister needed all these tests as she has been acting completely normal- she just has a cut on her forehead and i wasn't sure if it'd scar. np asked when the fall occured and i told her it was 10 am (this was about 11 hours later), and she responded she didn't realize. i asked if they would give my sister treatment without all these diagnostics tests and the np said that they would not! we felt stuck at that point, because the stitches needed to be done within a certain time frame. after all of this, we to the front and get called back again-they decided to finally take vitals/check the blood pressure of the girl who fainted! they also said they needed to take do a cat scan of her head! at this point, we refused treatment to the tech and said we needed to see an md/physician. the ct tech said okay and said we could go back out front. over an hour later, we were called back so more blood could be drawn; i asked if there was something wrong with the first draw, and was told no- they simply have to draw blood for the particular test over a period of six hours. we inquired as to why this was necessary and where the doctor was and why this was all needed for some stitches! the np came and said she was waiting on the cat scan results before she did stitches. we asked her who was ordering all these tests, and we absolutely refuse to have a cat scan. she said the doctor ordered them and we'd have to sign a waiver saying we decline treatment. we said we would like to see the doctor who is ordering these tests, because why is he/she doing so without even seeing the patient. she said she was ordering on behalf of the doctor. we proceeded to sternly say we need to see a doctor, and her response was, "well i see patients all the time by myself." we replied that was fine but we need to see a doctor. in the meantime, she went back to her office and we heard her talking to the doctor on speakerphone who said that we did not need to sign anything, but simply make sure it was noted in the chart. after some time we were put in a room, and then waited for the doctor. 
the poor doctor came in a while later and was very sweet. i was ready to just have my sister receive treatment and leave, but my mother said it was important to tell/ask about what happened because other patients need protection to. i then went into detail of everything happened, and said i felt the chest x-ray was completely unnecessary, i was appalled that the blood pressure of a patient who came in because she fainted was taken after having a chest x ray, and the bedside manner and advanced terminology of the np (kim tarver) was unacceptable. very surprisingly, the doctor agreed. she professionally stated she agreed that the chest xray was unnecessary and my sister did not need a cat scan. she said the blood pressure thing was an outlier, but still needed to be noted...and she stated the terminology used was a personnel issue. after all this, she used liquid stitches (liquid skin) on my sister. she's good to go now, but it was an incredibly painful, unnecessary process.

my husband has been a patient at mj several times. the first time, mj was an independent facility. therapists and nursing staff were both wonderful; efficient, well-trained and competent, very caring, and seemingly happy in their positions. in 2018 northwestern bought the facility. the facility has become very "corporate." while the therapy is still top-notch, the staff has taken on a different attitude toward their patients and their jobs. they are no longer caring and friendly; those traits enhance the patient and family experience and speed the healing process - lack of those traits make the patient want to get out of there before they are actually ready. the nursing staff, particularly the night shift, are "businesslike" to the point of being rude. the medical staff is also poor, at best, in communicating with patients and family and seem incompetent in following the discharge orders of the hospital from which the patient came, even to the point of simply ignoring the medication orders without informing the ordering physician or the patient/family. 
i am so disappointed that a superior facility like marianjoy would "sell out" to the corporate world which is taking over so much of medicine today. i would still return to mj strictly for the therapy, but i am certainly not happy about the new atmosphere and i honestly don't know if i would blanketly recommend the facility as i once did. 
i find that outpatient therapy at a dupage medical group facility is as good if the patient is capable of doing op therapy.
of course, there are still several staff members who maintain the old fashioned bedside manner and at least try to go above and beyond in patient care, but even those seem to be "afraid of breaking corporate protocol."

the second time (for the flu) we were seeing right away, we put masks on as soon as we walked in the door. for courtesy of other patient's. she was taken back to fast track. everything was fine until after the doctor came in, ran some tests, then sat us in this large common area full of other sick people and not a single person was wearing a mask! the two children that were sitting next to us were both diagnosed with the flu, and the only reason why i knew that is because one of the nurses came out and said it in front of everybody! the lady across from us also had the flu! no mask! how are you going to sit all these people in a large common area knowing they have the flu but not requiring them to wear a mask and infect the elderly patients that are also sitting in that waiting room, knowing that their immune system's are compromised because of age!?! my daughter and i were the only ones wearing a mask and it's not because they asked us. it's because i made that choice. 

that whole system they have is completely ridiculous and needs to be redone. out of respect for other patients and their privacy. 

most of the time the doctors and nurses are great, just depends on when you go i suppose.

do not go here!! if i could give negative stars i would!  i never take the time to write reviews but as a new mother i feel this is absolutely necessary for other mothers. most of our staff were fantastic and this review has no reflection on them what so ever. my baby caught rsv virus at 3 weeks old. we were transported via ambulance to summerlin hospital. 

first issue: food! as a nursing mother i need food and nutrition and they completely dropped the ball  on this. i didn't receive dinner until 8pm the first night my baby was admitted. next day, i didn't receive dinner at all. i called to complained to nutritionist the next morning about it and  also complained about the fact i was never given a choice of what food i wanted either. the following day my food came extremely late and it was the wrong order. i called to complain once again and she told me she resent it and i didn't get my breakfast until 1115am! the day after that they messed up my breakfast order again!!! they said it "got lost" and they were "sorry" and again i received breakfast around 1045am! my baby was deathly ill and the last thing i should have to worry about is calling and hunting down food for myself as i'm nursing my sick baby. 

second issue: one of the nurses. my baby started having a coughing spell around 12pm one night and was turning red and actually chocking because he couldn't breathe. i called the nurse immediately. she turned his oxygen up a bit and left the room. our baby continued coughing uncontrollably to where my husband and i thought he was for sure going to stop breathing (because that happened the previous day). we voiced concerns with nurse and she insisted we just keep him propped up to help control chocking and coughing. we told her this was not okay and he needed help as he was literally
gasping for air. we asked for pediatrician. nurse told us they always do a big consultation with the group as pediatricians need sleep between shifts. can you believe that!!! our baby was literally beat red gasping for air and the nurse didn't want to contact the pediatrician because they were sleeping between shifts?!!!! my husband told her to get pediatrician on the phone now. she did. pediatrician advised nurse to crank my babies oxygen to 8 and about blew my babies nostrils out of his head which caused him to cry and become even more hysterical than he already was which led to even more difficulty breathing and even more chocking!!!! we yelled at nurse to get pediatrician again! pediatrician said she wasn't going to give him anything for his cough! respiratory lady came in and instantly said he needed to be on a different breathing machine and she transferred us to another room asap!!! if we didn't push and be stern with the nurse to wake the damn pediatrician up and make a stink about all of this who knows what would have happened to our baby! thank god for respiratory nurse! to top all of that nightmare off the same nurse put in his new oxygen tube in his nose backwards so it was shooting air up and out of his nose instead back into his nose!!

third issue: sewage gas leakage!! yes a sewage leakage in the middle of all of this! we woke up to a foul smell and my grandmother fanning out 


last issue: the last issue was the cleanliness. my room was absolutely disgusting and the janitor didn't come by for a full day to empty the trash and it was actually overflowing along with trash everywhere on the floor! the head nurse finally came in and took it out and even he was pissed about it! whatever you do don't go here! it's one thing dealing with a sick baby but it's another when you cant event trust the hospital to look after your sick baby!

okay i understand couple 3 hours in the er naturally, 6 i repeat 6 hours later! mind you, my baby was freezing, she broke her leg at cheer i was not prepared for a cold all night stay in the er, i asked repeatedly for a blanket, we slept snuggled on a couch thing they have, and i watched her breathing all night because i was afraid of shock.

so, i asked, if i were about to have a heart attack? or had been shot?

then, two 80 year olds who were reported as having fevers, who were actively coughing and who seemed weak, were brought in in wheelchairs.

my mom fell this week (fragile, dementia, history of stroke, and a hip replacement). i called 911 and on scene the paramedics asked which hospital we preferred- i chose mercy general as her pcp and records are all at dignity health. 

worst decision ever. 
how the hospital is run: 
a doctor saw my mom for a total of 1 minute at arrival and 30 seconds at exit. no supervision or accountability. lots of people here seemed "checked out" working in an untenable environment. 

medical assistants and one rn is on duty, one pa or doctor for what seemed to be 50 or more patients. there are lots of guys in green outfits doing, apparently, nothing that i noticed for the five hours we were there. my mom was parked on a gurney for the whole time in a busy hallway. people, patients, staff, gurneys, paramedics, security guards, and random people coming and going nonstop. 

she had imaging of her hip, elbow, and arm. there were good people doing the imaging. i repeated that her head hurt- mom chimed in- and then that was related to the doctor and a ct was ordered. too bad the doctor refused to talk to the patient and just felt  her bones for minute and didn't ask one question to her "patient" aka just a number.  props to the imaging team for maintaining a system and compassion for patients in a totally chaotic situation. 

she was offered a tylenol and glass of water. no updates on what was happening...i assumed a room would be provided eventually.  other patients parked in hallway, including a man and his wife- he begged to have someone help her use the restroom- for an hour. 

at about 8:30 pm the medical assistant popped by and said no broken bones, mom had to get up and prove she could walk before being released. i stepped in when mom got upright on the gurney and said she felt dizzy. 

medical assistant said she would have a chair behind mom as she walks. my dad was helping. honest to god, this was the plan. my mom fell, said she's dizzy, and they want her to walk in a busy hallway with people crashing around pell-mell. 

i spoke up loudly, said you need to get an orderly and she said, this is how we do it do you have a better suggestion? 

this could have been solved by having my mom move to a room- (literally across the hall an empty room with three hospital beds) for a safe environment for a trial run. 

we worked with situation at hand with me guarding the hall like a pit bull behind mom and blocking people and gurneys from coming through....and dad ready to catch mom. and then medical assistant tells mom to get back to 
the gurney after a successful trial run. mom has lymphedema and her swollen legs would be hitting metal. i said no get a wheelchair. then a guy in green shows up. apparently ready to catch mom if she falls. thanks, perfect timing. 

so, end of story- doctor comes by for 30 seconds to tell us no broken bones and runs off, totally masked  to protect herself from coronavirus. brava. medical assistant turned out to be a nice person and she stood by us while my dad got car. she was smart and empathetic once she was freed from caring for 50 people simultaneously with no tangible support.

the main reason for this post is that the er staff mishandled information that caused them to break hipaa and i now have the personal information of a previous patient of this hospital. i do not believe this was intentional, but was a very careless mistake. there were several instances where this could have been caught prior to myself noticing it at the end of our visit. 

on tuesday morning 2/18 my boyfriend was not well and asked to be taken to the er and we went to broward hospital imperial point. due to his level of pain he was distracted and asked if i could handle the signing in and provided at check in with his driver's license and completed the intake form. 

after maybe 10 minutes the nurses came in to set my boyfriend up with an iv drip, etc. we were seen by the er doctor/pa (john marini), who came in to talk to my boyfriend who was in a lot of pain so i was assisting with some of the questions. due to where the pain was located the doctor ordered for an ultrasound of his abdomen and morphine for the pain. 

question #1: why are basic questions not being asked prior to ordering expensive tests? it is the middle of flu season and patient comes in with abdominal pain after vomiting for 5 hours. no pain over mcburney's point. at no time during the entire visit did anyone ask about if he had the flu shot, would he like a flu shot, or do any kind of test swabs for the flue.  immediately they went for more expensive tests. 

the er doctor/pa came to discuss that it looked like from the ultrasound that something with his gallbladder and pancreas, and that he wanted to order a ct scan. at this time another girl, administrative, rolled in a cart with a computer and began to go over basic patient information, much of what i had literally just filled out on the intake form or could be found on his license. doctor/pa was still present, as well as another nurse. 

the girl went through the list - name, birthday, address, emergency contact, etc. none of the information that they had on file was what i had filled out and we didn't recognize anything...

question #2: is it not protocol to ask the patients for their birthday and then the patient provides it? this girl was literally reading off what was on file, and each item we had no idea where that information was coming from. they had the wrong address, wrong birthday, we had never heard of the person that was the emergency contact. at no point during this initial confirmation of information did anyone ask him for his ssn, or i'm sure this would have been caught immediately. 

they took my boyfriend for a ct and he eventually returned. the doctor/pa returned to let us know that it didn't show any issues, that his gallbladder was contracted and nothing wrong with his pancreas (not shocking, ordered an expensive test for nothing without checking off all of the other things that it could be first). he would get us set up to be discharged. he also made some kind of comment that my boyfriend had been to the er back in 2015, which my boyfriend has never been there. 

while we continued to wait and i was holding my boyfriend's hand, at that point i noticed that the birthday on his wristband was incorrect. and that was when it clicked in my head that they 100% had some other patient's information and did not have the right patient. 

i went up to the girl who had been confirming all the information before and told her "the birthday on his wristband is wrong. when we were going over information before, we didn't know the emergency contact, you had the wrong address and phone number, are you sure  you have the right person?". she looked concerned and rolled her computer back in. now, finally, one of the first questions that she asked was for him to confirm the last 4 digits of his ssn. when he did, her eyes got wide with an 'oh s***' kind of look. so i directly asked her "is what i think is happening actually happening?" and she quietly said that she thought that i was right. i asked if that changed anything that had just happened here today, and she said "it doesn't change anything for you guys but it changes a lot for me" and rolled her little cart out. i have no idea if she fixed it or if she reported it.

this is long but bare with me. this place stereotypes people with mental health history. this is strictly for their er doctors and er intake nurses (some). i have past heart problems which were corrected in high school. i was feeling close to the same way the first time i had my heart episode and went to the er in mid november. i went in for heart palpitations, shortness of breath, extreme lethargic about to pass out feeling, and weakness. when i was taken to the er by my boyfriend, because who wants to call an ambulance on their lunch break in their work parking garage and drawl that kind of attention to themselves, when i got there, the intake nurses literally did not fucking care i existed as a human. it took the nurses or security guards who help wheel people in and out to tell them to open the door and let me in. the er intake nurse didn't give rats a$$ that i couldn't breath well, didn't pay attention to my boyfriend who was literally handing her an emergency card i keep in my wallet of all my allergies and medical history. my boyfriend told them my symptoms, they didn't even think about hooking me up to a ekg until i was in the er exam room, which if i can remember correctly was about 15 to 20 minutes after i arrived. the nurses were ok that day and the nurse who put my iv in kept moving it because she couldn't get the blood out...ok we'll go somewhere else?! so much pain while feeling like i could pass out. 

next the doctor comes in. talks about my symptoms, some history, so on. the moment i mentioned i was on an anti depressant with past history of anxiety, it switched his questions. it went from asking about how i was feeling physically to asking me if i was stressed, or sad, or anxious...so on with the other related questions. look, doc, i know the difference between heart problems and an anxiety attack, this is not an anxiety attack. so instead of ordering more tests he gives me an anti anxiety med, and let's me chill out for an hour or so. of course a anxiety med like xanax is going to chill me out and slow down my heart and breathing. been on them before in high school and anyone who has a friend in their residency at a top tier hospital can tell you, "yea that med is going to make your heart slow down and relax any symptoms." never once consulted a on staff cardiologist or offering to wait to have one come down because of my past history. given my previous heart problem, if anyone remotely understands the heart knows that things can come back and not in the same way as before!!! after this i was discharged and told if i have any more symptoms to come back. 

the next day and a half i slept, no joke, 18 hours out of a 24 hour day. i could still feel heart beats skip, still had shortness of breath just doing small things like going up stairs or even getting up to go to the bathroom. i didn't want to eat or even talk. so after a day and a half of not feeling like a functioning person, i went back.

this time the intake nurses took me seriously, hooked me up to ekg right away, and got an iv in me right away. this doctor took me seriously and ordered a ct with contrast to check for blood clots and did a few blood pressure tests based on laying and standing. everything came back normal. the moment i knew she looked at the most recent visit, started the, "are you sure you're not anxious," questions came out. in my head i'm thinking, "are you flipping kidding me?! does no one take me seriously?!" the one thing i will never forget the doctor saying to me is, " if you are feeling bad and don't get answers the first time, you shouldn't come back to the er. go see the doctors we referred you to the first time." i'm sorry what!????! i was literally doing what the discharge papers said. it's not my problem ( well kinda is if i die from not well examined heart issue) if you didn't exhaust all your resources to help or passed me along because you gave up. i started to cry. the only person who gave me hope was the nurse. she literally ask me, "do you feel safe to go home?" i flat out started crying, and said no. and told her i would never return here for any emergency. i told her i rather drive to a further hospital and die on the way, than come to this hospital again. she took that seriously and comforted me. i was discharged sent home waiting to see a cardiologist 2 weeks later. 

that cardiologist was pissed no one consulted a cardiologist on staff. i got an eco, heart monitor for a week, and a stress test, i have a problem with my sinus node and will need to have surgery. something that could have been solved and found in that moment if someone didn't profile me as a depressed anxious person!!! 

seriously, tell your doctors to stop stereotyping people with mental health problems. stop thinking that someone with a valid history of cardiac problems and a mental health past is just making it up and is just "anxious."
